entries.title: Acronyms (Chapter Glossary)
do_not_test: Acronym list itself - reference material only, not an independently testable competency.
entries.zero_question_reason: Pure glossary/reference content, no clinical competency to assess.

entries.title: Skin Anatomy, Function, and Age-Related Changes

testable_competencies.anatomy_framing: Recognize normal skin layer anatomy (epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous tissue) and epidermal appendages as background for interpreting abnormal skin findings.

entries.zero_question_reason: Normal anatomy/physiology background; not independently testable as a clinical presentation, but retained as scope for framing morphology-based questions elsewhere in the chapter.

entries.title: Approach to Skin Lesions: Morphology, Distribution, and Differential Diagnosis of Common Presentations

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to interpret 'critical clinical findings...from a general physical examination and an assessment of the skin characteristics (e.g., morphology and distribution)' - a direct textual match to this unit's content (primary/secondary lesion morphology, pattern/distribution terminology, and morphology-based differential diagnosis). This is the diagnostic-reasoning skill underlying essentially every other unit in the chapter rather than a single named diagnosis, so mapped as COMPONENT/MODERATE rather than DIRECT.

testable_competencies.lesion_description: Describe a skin lesion using standard morphologic terms (macule, papule, plaque, vesicle, bulla, pustule, wheal, etc.) and distribution/pattern descriptors.
testable_competencies.morphology_to_ddx: Generate a limited differential diagnosis for a described lesion morphology (e.g., vesicle, bulla, pustule, oral ulcer) using infectious, inflammatory, drug/toxin, and miscellaneous categories.

entries.title: Cysts (Epidermal, Pilar, Dermoid, Milium)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions list includes 'Tumours - Benign' explicitly; cyst clinical recognition and elective-excision-vs-observation management is a component of the general skin-and-integument presentation objective rather than a dedicated objective of its own.

testable_competencies.cyst_recognition: Distinguish common benign cutaneous cysts (epidermal, pilar, dermoid, milium) by clinical features and site, and recognize which require no treatment versus elective excision.

entries.title: Benign Fibrous and Hyperkeratotic Skin Lesions (Dermatofibroma, Skin Tags, Seborrheic Keratosis, Corns, Keloids)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions explicitly lists 'Tumours - Benign'; dermatofibroma, skin tags, seborrheic keratosis, corns, and keloids are all benign/reactive skin growths a graduating student must distinguish from premalignant/malignant lesions, which is the objective's stated key task ('determine whether a condition is benign, malignant, or associated with an underlying systemic condition').

testable_competencies.benign_growth_recognition: Recognize common benign skin growths (dermatofibroma, skin tag, seborrheic keratosis, corn, keloid) by characteristic clinical features and distinguish them from premalignant/malignant mimics (e.g., Leser-Trelat sign as a paraneoplastic clue).
testable_competencies.keloid_vs_scar: Distinguish keloid from hypertrophic scar based on extension beyond the original injury margin.

entries.title: Pigmented Nevi and Acquired Pigmented Lesions

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38 lists 'Tumours - Benign' and 'Premalignant' among causal_conditions and states the key task as determining whether a lesion is benign, malignant, or systemic; atypical/dysplastic nevus recognition (a melanoma risk marker) is the clinically highest-yield content in this unit.

testable_competencies.nevus_recognition: Distinguish benign congenital and acquired nevi from atypical/dysplastic nevi requiring surveillance or biopsy, using ABCDE-type features.
testable_competencies.pigmented_lesion_workup: Recognize when a changing or atypical pigmented lesion warrants excisional biopsy versus reassurance/photographic follow-up.

entries.title: Vascular Lesions and Malformations (Hemangioma, Vascular Malformations, Spider/Cherry Angioma, Pyogenic Granuloma)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38 lists 'Tumours - Vascular' among causal_conditions; infantile hemangioma recognition (including red-flag features requiring specialist referral) and distinguishing benign vascular lesions from concerning ones is core general-practice content.

testable_competencies.hemangioma_recognition: Recognize infantile hemangioma and its natural history, and identify features warranting early specialist referral (functional impairment, ulceration, high-risk location).
testable_competencies.vascular_lesion_ddx: Distinguish common benign vascular lesions (spider angioma, cherry angioma, pyogenic granuloma, port-wine stain) by clinical features.

entries.title: Lipoma and Xanthoma

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both are benign soft-tissue/lipid-deposit skin lesions within objective 38's 'Tumours - Benign' causal_conditions category; xanthoma additionally serves as a cutaneous marker of an underlying systemic condition (dyslipidemia), matching the objective's stated task of determining systemic association.

testable_competencies.lipoma_recognition: Recognize lipoma as a soft, mobile, non-tender subcutaneous mass requiring no treatment unless symptomatic or diagnostically uncertain.
testable_competencies.xanthoma_workup: Recognize xanthoma variants as potential cutaneous markers of dyslipidemia or hematologic disease and order a fasting lipid panel accordingly.

entries.title: Acne Vulgaris

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions list includes 'Papular' and 'Pustular' rashes; acne vulgaris is the prototypical high-prevalence example and its stepwise topical/systemic management (retinoid backbone, antibiotics, hormonal therapy, isotretinoin precautions) directly matches the objective's enabling-objective requirement to 'construct an effective management plan, including prescribe an appropriate topical and/or systemic therapy.'

testable_competencies.acne_grading: Grade acne severity (comedonal to nodulocystic) and select first-line topical versus systemic therapy accordingly.
testable_competencies.isotretinoin_safety: Recognize isotretinoin's key safety requirements (pregnancy exclusion/contraception counselling, baseline lipid/LFT monitoring).

entries.title: Perioral Dermatitis and Rosacea

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both are papulopustular facial dermatoses within objective 38's causal_conditions ('Papular', 'Pustular'); their DDx overlaps with acne vulgaris, and rosacea management (trigger avoidance, topical/oral antibiotics, laser for telangiectasia/phyma) matches the objective's management-planning enabling objective.

testable_competencies.rosacea_vs_acne: Distinguish rosacea from acne vulgaris (absence of comedones, central-face predilection, flushing) and from perioral dermatitis.
testable_competencies.rosacea_management: Select an appropriate first-line topical or oral therapy for rosacea based on predominant feature (erythema/telangiectasia vs. papulopustular vs. phymatous).

entries.title: Atopic Dermatitis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions explicitly include the 'Rashes' category and its enabling objectives require history/exam-based diagnosis plus a management plan; atopic dermatitis is Toronto Notes' most extensively developed single dermatitis subtype (dedicated pathophysiology, epidemiology, and a full stepwise treatment-ladder figure), warranting DIRECT rather than COMPONENT.

testable_competencies.ad_diagnosis: Recognize atopic dermatitis by age-dependent distribution, chronic pruritic course, and associated atopic history (asthma, allergic rhinitis, filaggrin-related xerosis).
testable_competencies.ad_stepwise_management: Select management by severity using the stepwise ladder: emollients/trigger avoidance -> topical corticosteroids or calcineurin inhibitors -> systemic/biologic therapy for refractory disease.

entries.title: Other Eczematous Dermatoses (Contact, Dyshidrotic, Nummular, Seborrheic, Stasis, Asteatotic Dermatitis; Lichen Simplex Chronicus)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions list 'Rashes' broadly including papular/vesiculobullous presentations; these seven dermatitis subtypes share a common inflammatory-eczema framework (irritant/allergic exposure, barrier dysfunction, or venous insufficiency) and overlapping first-line management (moisturization, topical corticosteroids), so are grouped as one COMPONENT unit rather than the chapter's single DIRECT eczema unit (Atopic Dermatitis, SU-D-11).

testable_competencies.eczema_subtype_ddx: Distinguish contact (irritant vs. allergic), dyshidrotic, nummular, seborrheic, stasis, and asteatotic dermatitis by distribution and clinical features, and select an appropriate first-line topical therapy.
testable_competencies.irritant_vs_allergic_contact: Differentiate irritant from allergic contact dermatitis by mechanism, time course, and role of patch testing.

entries.title: Papulosquamous Diseases: Lichen Planus and Pityriasis Rosea

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both are named 'Rashes' within objective 38's causal_conditions; Lichen Planus's classic morphology (6 Ps, Wickham's striae) and Pityriasis Rosea's herald patch/Christmas-tree distribution are both classic, frequently-tested pattern-recognition presentations.

testable_competencies.lichen_planus: Recognize lichen planus by the '6 Ps' morphology and Wickham's striae, and know its association with hepatitis C.
testable_competencies.pityriasis_rosea: Recognize pityriasis rosea by herald patch followed by a Christmas-tree-pattern truncal eruption and manage expectantly (self-limited).

entries.title: Psoriasis (Plaque, Guttate, Erythrodermic, Pustular, Inverse) and Systemic Therapy

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Psoriasis is explicitly a named 'Rash' under objective 38's causal_conditions, and its severity-stratified topical/phototherapy/systemic/biologic management ladder is a direct, extensively detailed match to the objective's enabling requirement to 'construct an effective management plan, including prescribe appropriate topical and/or systemic therapy' and to 'refer if appropriate.'

testable_competencies.psoriasis_recognition: Recognize plaque psoriasis (well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale, Auspitz sign, extensor/scalp/nail distribution) and its guttate, erythrodermic, pustular, and inverse variants.
testable_competencies.psoriasis_severity_management: Select management by disease severity (BSA/PASI): topical therapy for mild disease, phototherapy or systemic/biologic therapy for moderate-severe disease; recognize erythrodermic and generalized pustular psoriasis as potentially life-threatening requiring urgent management.

entries.title: Psoriatic Arthritis (cross-reference to Rheumatology)

testable_competencies.psa_risk_marker: Recognize nail or scalp psoriasis involvement as a risk marker for psoriatic arthritis and refer/screen accordingly; full joint-disease diagnosis and management belongs to Rheumatology.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Primary clinical content (arthritis pattern recognition, DMARD/biologic management) belongs to the Rheumatology chapter (Toronto Notes cross-reference: 'see Rheumatology, RH25'); this Dermatology unit covers only the dermatologic risk-marker recognition task.

entries.title: Bullous Pemphigoid

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions explicitly list 'Vesiculobullous' among rash categories; bullous pemphigoid is the prototypical elderly-onset autoimmune bullous disease and a classic exam topic for distinguishing tense subepidermal bullae from pemphigus vulgaris's flaccid intraepidermal bullae (SU-D-17).

testable_competencies.bp_diagnosis: Recognize bullous pemphigoid by tense subepidermal bullae in an elderly patient and immunofluorescence showing linear IgG/C3 at the basement membrane.
testable_competencies.bp_vs_pv: Distinguish bullous pemphigoid (deeper, tense bullae) from pemphigus vulgaris (superficial, flaccid bullae, mucosal involvement, positive Nikolsky sign).

entries.title: Pemphigus Vulgaris and Pemphigus Foliaceus

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches objective 38's 'Vesiculobullous' causal_conditions category; pemphigus vulgaris is a classic, potentially fatal autoimmune blistering disease requiring prompt recognition and immunosuppressive treatment, matching the objective's management-planning enabling objective.

testable_competencies.pv_diagnosis: Recognize pemphigus vulgaris by flaccid, non-pruritic, predominantly mucosal-onset bullae, positive Nikolsky sign, and anti-desmoglein-1/3 IgG on immunofluorescence.
testable_competencies.pv_management: Recognize that pemphigus vulgaris requires prompt systemic immunosuppression and can be fatal if untreated, unlike the generally self-limited course of most other vesiculobullous rashes.

entries.title: Dermatitis Herpetiformis and Porphyria Cutanea Tarda

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both are vesiculobullous/papulovesicular rashes within objective 38's causal_conditions with important underlying-systemic-disease associations (celiac disease; hepatitis C, alcohol use, and estrogen therapy respectively), matching the objective's task of determining systemic association.

testable_competencies.dh_recognition: Recognize dermatitis herpetiformis as the cutaneous marker of celiac disease and its dapsone/gluten-free-diet management.
testable_competencies.pct_recognition: Recognize porphyria cutanea tarda by photo-exposed skin fragility/bullae and its associations with hepatitis C, alcohol use, and estrogen therapy.

entries.title: Drug Eruptions: Exanthematous Reaction and DRESS/DIHS

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions list 'Toxic' reactions and 'Rashes'; morbilliform drug eruption is the most common cutaneous drug reaction, and DRESS is a can't-miss severe drug reaction (fever + rash + eosinophilia + internal organ involvement) matching the objective's task of recognizing severity/complications.

testable_competencies.exanthematous_recognition: Recognize morbilliform exanthematous drug eruption by time course (7-14 d after drug start) and common causative agents (penicillin, sulfonamides, phenytoin).
testable_competencies.dress_recognition: Recognize DRESS/DIHS as a can't-miss severe drug reaction (fever, morbilliform rash, facial edema, eosinophilia, internal organ involvement) requiring prompt drug discontinuation.

entries.title: Drug-Induced Urticaria/Angioedema and Serum Sickness-Like Reaction

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Drug-induced urticaria/angioedema is a directly named clinical scenario within objective 97-2 ('Urticaria, angioedema'), whose causal_conditions explicitly list 'Allergic (e.g., drugs...)' and whose enabling objectives require detecting the risk of anaphylaxis/laryngeal edema - matching this unit's content on second-most-common drug-reaction recognition and epinephrine/antihistamine management.

testable_competencies.drug_urticaria_recognition: Recognize drug-induced urticaria/angioedema and assess for concurrent anaphylaxis (bronchospasm, laryngeal edema, shock) requiring emergency management.
testable_competencies.serum_sickness: Recognize serum sickness-like reaction (symmetrical urticarial eruption, malaise, arthralgia 1-3 wk after drug exposure) and distinguish it from true serum sickness.

entries.title: Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis (AGEP)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A named 'Toxic'/'Pustular' rash category under objective 38's causal_conditions; AGEP is a distinct severe cutaneous adverse reaction commonly tested against pustular psoriasis and SJS/TEN in the differential.

testable_competencies.agep_recognition: Recognize AGEP by rapid onset of extensive sterile pustules with high fever and neutrophilia after a causative drug, and distinguish it from generalized pustular psoriasis and SJS/TEN.

entries.title: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (SJS/TEN)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: SJS/TEN is explicitly a 'Bullous' rash under objective 38's causal_conditions and exemplifies the objective's key task of determining 'severity and complications' and initiating urgent management; its mortality (5% SJS, 30% TEN) and named-drug/HLA risk factors make it one of the highest-yield can't-miss topics in the chapter.

testable_competencies.sjs_ten_recognition: Recognize SJS/TEN by prodromal targetoid/purpuric rash progressing to positive Nikolsky sign, full-thickness epidermal detachment, and mucosal erosions, and classify severity by percent BSA detachment.
testable_competencies.sjs_ten_management: Initiate immediate drug discontinuation and refer to an ICU/burn unit for supportive care; recognize high-risk causative drugs (allopurinol, anti-epileptics, sulfonamides) and associated HLA alleles.

entries.title: Fixed Drug Eruption and Photosensitivity Reaction

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both are 'Toxic'/drug-related rash presentations under objective 38's causal_conditions, grouped as one COMPONENT unit given their shorter, less independently high-yield content relative to SJS/TEN and DRESS.

testable_competencies.fde_recognition: Recognize fixed drug eruption by its hallmark recurrence at the same anatomic site on re-exposure to the causative drug.
testable_competencies.photosensitivity: Distinguish phototoxic (exaggerated sunburn, direct injury) from photoallergic (pruritic eczematous, type IV hypersensitivity) drug-induced photosensitivity reactions.

entries.title: Heritable Genodermatoses (Ichthyosis Vulgaris, Epidermolysis Bullosa, Oculocutaneous Albinism)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions do not name specific genodermatoses but do include general 'Rashes'/pigmentary categories; these three rare inherited disorders are lower-yield 'know it exists' content, mapped COMPONENT/MODERATE reflecting their status as classic-but-rare named entities rather than common general-practice presentations.

testable_competencies.genodermatosis_recognition: Recognize ichthyosis vulgaris (fish-scale xerosis, filaggrin gene), epidermolysis bullosa (trauma-induced blistering from birth), and oculocutaneous albinism as classic inherited skin disorders.

entries.title: Neurofibromatosis Type 1

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: A classic, frequently-tested single-gene disorder with defining cutaneous findings (cafe-au-lait macules, neurofibromas) that fall under objective 38's causal_conditions; the diagnostic-criteria checklist itself is a classic multiple-choice exam pattern.

testable_competencies.nf1_diagnosis: Apply the NF1 diagnostic criteria (>=2 of 7 features including cafe-au-lait macules >=6, neurofibromas, axillary/inguinal freckling, Lisch nodules, optic glioma) to diagnose neurofibromatosis type 1.

entries.title: Vitiligo

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions do not separately list 'depigmentation' but vitiligo is a common, highly recognizable rash/pigmentary presentation with a well-defined systemic-autoimmune-association workup matching the objective's enabling objectives on investigating for underlying systemic disease.

testable_competencies.vitiligo_workup: Recognize vitiligo (depigmented macules, Wood's lamp confirmation) and screen for associated autoimmune disease (thyroid disease, T1DM, Addison's, pernicious anemia).

entries.title: Bacterial Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (Impetigo, Erysipelas, Cellulitis, Folliculitis/Furuncle/Carbuncle, Skin Abscess)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions explicitly list 'Infectious' among rash/skin-condition categories; bacterial SSTI recognition (including the erysipelas-vs-cellulitis and folliculitis-vs-furuncle-vs-carbuncle distinctions and antibiotic selection) is core, high-frequency general-practice content.

testable_competencies.impetigo_recognition: Recognize impetigo by honey-crusted lesions and select topical vs. systemic antibiotics by extent.
testable_competencies.erysipelas_vs_cellulitis: Distinguish erysipelas (sharp raised border, upper dermis/lymphatics) from cellulitis (poorly demarcated, lower dermis/subcutaneous fat) and select first-line antibiotics.
testable_competencies.abscess_management: Recognize skin abscess and determine when incision-and-drainage alone suffices versus when adjunctive antibiotics are indicated.

entries.title: Dermatophyte Infections (Tinea Capitis, Corporis, Cruris, Pedis, Manuum, Unguium, Barbae)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches objective 38's 'Infectious' causal_conditions category and its enabling objective on investigations that 'differentiate benign from more serious disorders (e.g., biopsy, fungal scraping)' - KOH prep is the named example investigation. Tinea is extremely high-frequency general-practice/family-medicine content.

testable_competencies.tinea_site_recognition: Recognize the site-specific presentations of dermatophyte infection (tinea capitis with kerion, corporis, cruris, pedis, unguium) and select topical vs. oral antifungal therapy based on site and severity.
testable_competencies.koh_prep: Use KOH preparation of skin scrapings as the confirmatory investigation for suspected dermatophyte infection.

entries.title: Parasitic and Arthropod Skin Infestations (Scabies, Lice, Bed Bugs, Cutaneous Larva Migrans, Leishmaniasis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches objective 38's 'Infectious' causal_conditions; scabies in particular is a can't-miss, high-frequency diagnosis with a distinctive presentation (nocturnal pruritus, burrows, web-space distribution) and specific permethrin-based management and contact-treatment requirement.

testable_competencies.scabies_recognition: Recognize scabies by nocturnal pruritus, burrows in web spaces/flexures, and treat the patient plus close contacts with permethrin.
testable_competencies.lice_recognition: Recognize scalp/pubic/body lice by nits and excoriations and select permethrin-based treatment with environmental decontamination.

entries.title: Herpes Simplex Virus and Herpes Zoster Virus Infections

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches objective 38's 'Infectious' causal_conditions; HSV and HZV are extremely high-frequency presentations with distinctive vesicular morphology and well-defined antiviral management, plus HZV's vaccination-prevention angle matches the objective's counselling/prevention enabling objective.

testable_competencies.hsv_recognition: Recognize primary vs. recurrent HSV-1/HSV-2 by distribution and select appropriate oral antiviral therapy.
testable_competencies.hzv_recognition: Recognize herpes zoster by unilateral dermatomal vesicular eruption, identify Hutchinson's sign as indicating ocular involvement requiring urgent ophthalmology referral, and initiate antivirals within 72 hours.
testable_competencies.hzv_prevention: Recommend recombinant zoster vaccine for prevention in patients >=50 years.

entries.title: Molluscum Contagiosum and Cutaneous HPV (Warts)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Both are common viral 'Infectious' skin conditions under objective 38; genital warts (condyloma acuminata) additionally carry oncogenic-HPV-subtype counselling relevance matching the objective's education/prevention enabling objective.

testable_competencies.molluscum_recognition: Recognize molluscum contagiosum as a self-limited viral infection and select observation vs. destructive therapy.
testable_competencies.wart_recognition: Distinguish verruca vulgaris, plantaris, and condyloma acuminata by site and morphology, and counsel on HPV subtypes associated with cervical/anogenital dysplasia.

entries.title: Superficial Yeast Infections (Candidiasis, Tinea Versicolor)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches objective 38's 'Infectious' causal_conditions; candidal intertrigo and tinea versicolor are both high-frequency primary-care presentations with distinctive clinical features and topical antifungal management.

testable_competencies.candidal_intertrigo: Recognize candidal intertrigo by satellite pustules in skin folds and identify predisposing factors (obesity, diabetes, antibiotics, immunosuppression).
testable_competencies.tinea_versicolor: Recognize pityriasis (tinea) versicolor by hypo-/hyperpigmented scaling macules that fail to tan, and treat with topical/systemic antifungals.

entries.title: Cutaneous Manifestations of Sexually Transmitted Infections (Syphilis, Gonococcemia)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches objective 38's 'Infectious' causal_conditions category; the staged syphilis presentation (chancre -> secondary rash -> gumma) is a classic high-yield pattern-recognition topic with public-health reporting relevance.

testable_competencies.syphilis_staging: Recognize the staged presentation of syphilis (painless chancre -> secondary maculopapular/condyloma lata rash -> tertiary gumma) and select penicillin G-based treatment by stage.
testable_competencies.gonococcemia_recognition: Recognize disseminated gonococcal infection by hemorrhagic pustules on a purpuric background with arthritis/tenosynovitis, and initiate ceftriaxone with STI screening and public health notification.

entries.title: Pre-Malignant Skin Conditions (Actinic Keratosis, Leukoplakia)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions explicitly list 'Premalignant' as a named category and the key_objectives text states the central task is to 'determine whether a condition is benign, malignant or associated with an underlying systemic condition' - a direct match to actinic keratosis's role as a precursor requiring monitoring/treatment to prevent progression to SCC.

testable_competencies.ak_recognition: Recognize actinic keratosis (rough erythematous scaly papule on sun-damaged skin) as a premalignant lesion and select appropriate field or lesion-directed treatment.
testable_competencies.leukoplakia_recognition: Recognize oral leukoplakia as a premalignant mucosal lesion requiring biopsy to exclude malignancy.

entries.title: Nonmelanoma Skin Cancers (Basal Cell Carcinoma, Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Bowen's Disease)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions explicitly name 'Malignant' tumours as a category (with 'e.g., melanoma' as the given example, implying non-melanoma skin cancer is included under the broader malignant-tumour task); BCC/SCC recognition and biopsy-driven management is core, high-frequency content given skin cancer's status as the most common cancer.

testable_competencies.bcc_recognition: Recognize basal cell carcinoma by pearly, telangiectatic, rolled-border papule/nodule and select biopsy/excision as management.
testable_competencies.scc_bowens_recognition: Recognize Bowen's disease (SCC in situ) and invasive SCC, and understand their progression risk and management (excision, electrodesiccation).

entries.title: Malignant Melanoma

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions list gives melanoma as the explicit worked example of a 'Malignant' skin tumour ('Malignant (e.g., melanoma)'), making this the single highest-confidence DIRECT mapping in the entire chapter.

testable_competencies.melanoma_recognition: Apply the ABCDE criteria to recognize a mole with malignant features and initiate urgent biopsy/referral.
testable_competencies.melanoma_risk: Recognize risk factors and monitoring requirements for melanoma (atypical/dysplastic nevi, family history, UV exposure).

entries.title: Other Cutaneous Cancers (Kaposi Sarcoma)
entries.zero_question_reason: Rare cutaneous malignancy (Kaposi sarcoma) typically associated with HIV/immunosuppression; specialist-level content beyond the general-practice recognition tasks already covered by the BCC/SCC/melanoma units.

entries.title: Alopecia (Non-Scarring and Scarring) and Hypertrichosis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions explicitly list 'Hair presentations - Alopecia - Scarring - Non-scarring - Hirsutism - Hypertrichosis' verbatim, a direct textual match to this unit's full content scope.

testable_competencies.alopecia_ddx: Distinguish non-scarring alopecia (telogen/anagen effluvium, alopecia areata, androgenic alopecia) from scarring alopecia by history, distribution, and follicular ostia preservation, and recognize scarring alopecia as requiring biopsy/dermatology referral.
testable_competencies.hypertrichosis_recognition: Recognize hypertrichosis as excessive hair growth independent of androgen effect, distinct from hirsutism.

entries.title: Nail Disorders and Primary Hyperhidrosis (Adnexal Disorders)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions explicitly list 'Nail presentations - Local nail problems - Associated with an underlying condition', a direct textual match; hyperhidrosis is grouped here as the chapter's other adnexal-structure disorder.

testable_competencies.nail_systemic_association: Recognize nail changes (e.g., pitting, onycholysis, yellow nail syndrome) as cutaneous markers of an underlying systemic or dermatologic condition using Table 24.
testable_competencies.hyperhidrosis_recognition: Recognize primary hyperhidrosis by focal, bilateral, waking-hours sweating without an underlying cause and select first-line management (antiperspirants, botulinum toxin).

entries.title: Oral Diseases (Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches objective 38's causal_conditions, which include oral-mucosal presentations implicitly through 'Rashes' generally; also overlaps with the dedicated 'Oral conditions' objective (MCC-60), whose causal_conditions explicitly list oral ulceration among acquired oral conditions.

testable_competencies.ras_recognition: Recognize recurrent aphthous stomatitis (canker sores) by painful, shallow, round-to-oval mucosal ulcers with a creamy-white pseudomembrane, and distinguish from Behcet syndrome/HSV in the differential.

entries.title: Skin Manifestations of Systemic Disease

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches objective 38's stated key task: 'it is important to determine whether a condition is benign, malignant or associated with an underlying systemic condition' - this unit's entire content is a systematic list of skin findings that signal an underlying systemic disease.

testable_competencies.skin_systemic_association: Recognize named cutaneous signs of systemic disease (e.g., dermatomyositis heliotrope rash/Gottron's papules, acanthosis nigricans as an insulin-resistance marker, Paget's disease of the nipple, necrobiosis lipoidica diabeticorum) and connect them to the underlying diagnosis.

entries.title: Angioedema, Urticaria, and Erythema Nodosum

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Angioedema/Urticaria is a directly dedicated MCC objective; this unit's content (hereditary vs. acquired angioedema, laryngeal-edema risk, urticaria classification by chronicity/mechanism, mastocytosis) matches the objective's causal_conditions and its enabling-objective emphasis on detecting cardio-respiratory distress/anaphylaxis risk and prescribing epinephrine when indicated.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Erythema nodosum (a panniculitis, not urticaria) is separately captured under objective 38's broader 'Rashes'/systemic-association causal_conditions, grouped into this unit given its short length and shared 'Miscellaneous Lesions' source section.

testable_competencies.angioedema_urticaria: Distinguish hereditary from acquired angioedema, recognize laryngeal-edema risk requiring epinephrine, and classify urticaria as acute vs. chronic with appropriate investigation.
testable_competencies.erythema_nodosum: Recognize erythema nodosum by tender, poorly-demarcated pretibial nodules and investigate for underlying causes (streptococcal infection, sarcoidosis, IBD, malignancy).

entries.title: Pruritus (Approach to Generalized Itch)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Directly matches the dedicated MCC objective 'Pruritus' (85); the unit's structure - differentiating pruritus with primary skin disease from pruritus with no skin lesions (dermatologic vs. hepatic/renal/hematologic/endocrine/psychiatric causes) - is a near word-for-word match to objective 85's key_objectives and enabling_objectives text.

testable_competencies.pruritus_approach: Differentiate pruritus with an identifiable primary skin lesion from generalized pruritus without skin lesions, and initiate an appropriate systemic workup (CBC, renal/hepatic function, TSH) for the latter.

entries.title: Wounds and Ulcers, and Pediatric Exanthems (Cross-References to Other Chapters)
entries.zero_question_reason: Pure cross-reference lines directing the reader to other chapters; no independent Dermatology-chapter content to test here.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Both headings are pure 'see [other chapter]' cross-references in the source text (Pediatric Exanthems -> Pediatrics P62; Wounds and Ulcers -> Plastic Surgery PL8) with no independent content in the Dermatology chapter; substantive coverage belongs to those chapters' own scope-mapping passes.

entries.title: Sun Protection and Photodamage (Sunscreens, Sunburn, UV Radiation)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's enabling objectives explicitly require 'offer counselling and education, including prevention of future skin conditions (e.g., sun exposure)' - a direct, near-verbatim textual match to this unit's sunscreen-counselling content.

testable_competencies.sun_counselling: Counsel patients on sun-protective behaviour and sunscreen selection (SPF, broad-spectrum, physical vs. chemical) as primary prevention for photodamage and skin cancer.

entries.title: Principles of Topical and Systemic Dermatologic Therapy
entries.zero_question_reason: Reference-table-level pharmacy detail (steroid potency rankings, specific product names/dosing) beyond general-practice scope; individual drug names/doses relevant to specific diagnoses are captured within each diagnosis's own study unit instead of duplicated here.

entries.title: Perniosis (Chilblains) and Traumatic/Mechanical Skin Disorders

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions list 'Toxic' and general rash/reaction categories under which cold-induced perniosis fits; the only substantive dermatology-specific content under this heading, so mapped DIRECT despite low overall coverage weight.

testable_competencies.perniosis_recognition: Recognize perniosis (chilblains) by erythematous-to-violaceous acral lesions after cold, damp, non-freezing exposure and manage with warming/avoidance.
